IFM Investors Pty Ltd lowered its position in shares of Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 0.9% during the 4th quarter, according to the company in its most recent filing with the Securities & Exchange Commission. The institutional investor owned 144,741 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after selling 1,308 shares during the quarter. Apple accounts for approximately 3.9% of IFM Investors Pty Ltd’s investment portfolio, making the stock its biggest holding. IFM Investors Pty Ltd’s holdings in Apple were worth $24,495,000 at the end of the most recent quarter.
Several other institutional investors have also recently bought and sold shares of the business. Capital Insight Partners LLC raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 4.9% in the 4th quarter. Capital Insight Partners LLC now owns 6,292 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $1,065,000 after purchasing an additional 293 shares during the period. Corundum Group Inc. raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 15.4% in the 3rd quarter. Corundum Group Inc. now owns 2,242 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $346,000 after purchasing an additional 299 shares during the period. Crossvault Capital Management LLC raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 0.5% in the 3rd quarter. Crossvault Capital Management LLC now owns 65,678 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $10,122,000 after purchasing an additional 300 shares during the period. Welch Investments LLC raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 18.7% in the 3rd quarter. WI now owns 76,786 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $12,994,000 after purchasing an additional 303 shares during the period. 61.18% of the stock is currently owned by hedge funds and other institutional investors. AAPL has been the topic of a number of research reports. Zacks Investment Research raised shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating and set a $190.00 price target on the stock in a report on Wednesday, January 3rd. Barclays set a $162.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the company a “neutral” rating in a report on Wednesday, January 3rd. UBS set a $190.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Friday, January 5th. Maxim Group boosted their target price on shares of Apple from $193.00 to $204.00 and gave the company a “buy” rating in a report on Friday, January 12th. Finally, Longbow Research cut shares of Apple from a “buy” rating to a “neutral” rating in a report on Wednesday, January 17th. Two analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have given a hold rating, thirty-three have issued a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the company. The company presently has an average rating of “Buy” and a consensus price target of $203.58. NASDAQ AAPL opened at $176.57 on Thursday. The company has a quick ratio of 1.20, a current ratio of 1.24 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.74. Apple has a 12-month low of $142.20 and a 12-month high of $183.50. The stock has a market cap of $858,015.69, a price-to-earnings ratio of 19.17, a price-to-earnings-growth ratio of 1.29 and a beta of 1.26.
Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last posted its quarterly earnings results on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, beating the consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.33%. The business had revenue of $61.14 billion during the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. During the same period in the prior year, the business posted $2.10 earnings per share. The company’s revenue was up 15.6% on a year-over-year basis. sell-side analysts predict that Apple will post 11.28 earnings per share for the current fiscal year.
The firm also recently declared a quarterly dividend, which will be paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th will be given a dividend of $0.73 per share. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.65%. This is a positive change from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date is Friday, May 11th. Apple’s dividend payout ratio is presently 27.36%.
Apple declared that its Board of Directors has approved a stock repurchase plan on Tuesday, May 1st that permits the company to buyback $100.00 billion in shares. This buyback authorization permits the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares buyback plans are usually an indication that the company’s management believes its stock is undervalued.

Following the completion of the transaction, the senior vice president now directly owns 66,191 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $11,194,221.92.
